As I'm sure you know, monetary policy—past, present, and future—plays an
important role in the outlook over the next year or so.
1.

During 1994 and early 1995, the Fed tightened policy in order to slow the
economy—
1.

and achieving that goal is the main way that monetary policy can
promote the maximum sustainable advance in the country's economic
output and the people's standard of living.

It can take anywhere from a year and a half to three years for a
monetary policy action to produce results on inflation.

This kind of time lag means that it's dangerous to wait until the problem
shows up in the inflation data—by then we'd be too late.

This brings me to my third point: the pressures for higher inflation intensify
the longer the economy operates beyond its long-run capacity to produce goods
and services.
1.

I'll start with a definition of the potential growth rate: It's the growth
rate an economy is capable of sustaining in the long run.

Obviously, monetary policy has little impact on these factors, so
it can't determine the potential growth rate;

The second key factor underlying the inflationary risks in the economy
is the so-called "natural rate of unemployment."
a.

This is the rate the economy can sustain in the long run, and it's
determined by current technology, labor market size and
composition, and so forth, in today's economy.
(1)

This rapid growth was great when the economy had plenty of excess
capacity coming out of the 1990-91 recession.

The unemployment rate fell from a peak of about IV2 percent to as low as 5Vi
percent,
1.

The first quarter numbers show that growth slowed substantially— from a 5
percent pace in the fourth quarter of 1994 to 2% percent.
1.

Since both sectors are sensitive to interest rates, this is exactly where a
slowdown induced by tighter monetary policy would be expected to
show up.

But, in part because of the continuing strength in business investment and
exports, I'd expect moderate growth to resume later this year.
1.

I think it's worth emphasizing that the Fed won't be focusing so much
on any individual quarter's performance as much as it will focus on the
longer-run average rate of growth.

a.

So although the national slowdown will have some effect, factors affecting the

For example, on the negative side, sagging employment in the oil sector,
